extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators and research administrators applying for NIH Research Supplements to Promote Diversity (and NIH program staff reviewing those requests)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guidance for NIH staff and PIs on preparing and evaluating requests for Research Supplements to Promote Diversity in Health-Related Research (add-on supplements to active parent awards such as R01). Covers candidate eligibility, review dimensions, administrative process, and strategic advice to strengthen requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the candidate's readiness and potential for research and career progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider career goals, prior research training, research potential, relevant experience, and academic record (note: academic record expectations vary by career stage). Evaluate how the candidate's background supports success in the proposed supplement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on the Parent Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how the proposed supplement activities increase or preserve the overall impact of the parent award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplement must stay within the original scope of the parent award (cannot expand scope). Reviewers assess the ability of the proposed activities to enhance the parent grant's scientific or training objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength of the plan describing how the appointment will promote diversity in biomedical, behavioral, or clinical research nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the description of how the candidate's appointment contributes to diversifying the research workforce, the plan for the candidate's training and career development, and the mentorship arrangements that support inclusion and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and suitability of the proposed research training experience within the supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the soundness of the proposed training/research experience, appropriateness of methods, and the relevance of the work to the parent grant. The research plan should be feasible as a training experience and well-integrated with the parent project's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the mentorship to be provided to the candidate by the PI and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the quality of mentorship by the PI, specificity of planned training activities, the plan for the candidate's professional development, and concrete career development opportunities. Mentorship plans should be specific and substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Review Process (no peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural note: diversity supplement requests are not subject to NIH peer review and are handled administratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement applications can be approved by NIH Project Officers, are supported by set-aside funds, and are reviewed internally for scientific merit and training potential. Prepare materials mindful of internal review expectations rather than standard peer review scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Candidate Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of individuals NIH is particularly interested in recruiting and retaining for these supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH is particularly interested in individuals from racial and ethnic groups shown to be underrepresented nationally: Blacks or African Americans; Hispanics or Latinos; American Indians or Alaska Natives; Native Hawaiians and other Pacific Islanders. Also eligible: individuals with disabilities and individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds (for some institutes). Use these categories when describing the candidate's eligibility and diversity contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Stage Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Which career stages are eligible for diversity supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible stages include high school students, undergraduate students, post-baccalaureate research education program participants, graduate students (predoctoral), postdoctoral fellows, and eligible faculty/investigators. Tailor the application (e.g., expectations, academic record evidence, career development plan) to the candidate's career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent Grant Eligibility / Eligible Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Which active parent awards qualify to receive a diversity supplement request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs generally eligible if they hold active R-series awards (R01, R34, R35, R37, etc.), P-series (P01, P30, P50, etc.), U-series cooperative agreements, some training grants, and certain specific mechanisms (e.g., some NCI mechanisms). Confirm mechanism-specific eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Considerations to Strengthen Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory guidance on features that make supplement requests more competitive or likely to be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger supplements clearly align the candidate's research with the parent grant aims; present a specific and substantive mentorship plan; match the career development plan to the candidate's career stage; include a letter of support from the candidate's department. Note that some parent grants may allow multiple supplements.
